clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old man presented with sudden paraplegia, bilateral leg pain, numbness, pallor, and absence of femoral and distal pulses, with metabolic acidosis and elevated lactate. Bedside ultrasound showed no free fluid and normal aorta. CT angiography confirmed extensive aortic thrombosis from the diaphragm to the bifurcation without atherosclerosis. Open surgical exploration identified visceral ischemia and endovascular thrombectomy and stenting of involved arteries were performed. After 3.5 months of inpatient rehabilitation, some sensory function returned but wheelchair dependency persisted.
